storyboard.ears: A child's whole future can depend on which country's classroom they land in.
India has 127.5 million secondary pupils, nearly double China. Education at this scale strains any school system.
storyboard.eyes: substance: pupils with backpacks; cause: Data drags the school's iron gate open by hand and the crowd waiting outside walks into the yard
storyboard.evidence: World Bank | General pupils secondary education | https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/SE.SEC.ENRL.GC | 2026-11-21

storyboard.ears: In Guinea-Bissau, one college teacher faces 147.6 students, more than double the next worst country. Individual attention becomes scarce.
Education spending fell to 3.57 percent of national income, the lowest in this data. Growing systems have less room to improve.
storyboard.evidence: World Bank | Total government expenditure on education | https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/SE.XPD.TOTL.GD.ZS | 2026-11-21

storyboard.ears: Today, 92 percent of young women can read, up from about two thirds in 1975. Wider access produced real gains.
storyboard.evidence: World Bank | Youth female literacy rate | https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/SE.ADT.1524.LT.FE.ZS | 2026-11-21

storyboard.ears: In Tanzania, one preschool teacher has 114 children, almost double the next worst country. The pressure starts before primary school.
Education grew, but scale still decides how much attention each student receives.
